# HConnectionState

> Connection lifecycle feedback with an optional application-owned retry action.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.5.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HConnectionState` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-connection-state>`.
- Constructor: `HearthConnectionStateElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Feedback.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HConnectionState.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- The app supplies connection state and performs retry. This component does not monitor connectivity or create timers.
- State text accompanies semantic color. Retry is offered for failed/offline states when retryable is enabled.

## Public API

state: connecting | connected | reconnecting | failed | offline · label, description: string · retryable: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    state?: "connecting" | "connected" | "reconnecting" | "failed" | "offline";
    label?: string;
    description?: string;
    retryable?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ state: "offline", label: "Connection", retryable: true }
```

### Events

retry()

```ts
type Emits = {
    retry: [
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, title, description

Use `hearth-connection-state::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HConnectionState } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
function retry() { /* Retry through the application connection service. */ }
</script>

<template>
  <HConnectionState state="failed" label="Docker provider" description="The endpoint is unreachable." @retry="retry" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-connection-state');
Object.assign(element, {
  "state": "failed",
  "label": "Docker provider",
  "description": "The endpoint is unreachable."
});

element.addEventListener('retry', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```

## Related components

- [HProviderSetup](../provider-setup/llms.txt): A connection setup recipe with required fields, test/save requests, and connection feedback.
- [HAlert](../alert/llms.txt): Inline feedback for success, information, and problems. Errors announce as alerts; other tones use status.
- [HBadge](../badge/llms.txt): A compact label with optional status dot. Color always accompanies text.
